findings.issue: Decision 11 states the production build is part of the verification gate for `.svelte` changes, alongside scenario coverage. Verified against `esbuild.config.mjs`/`esbuild.harness.mjs`: `esbuild-svelte` with `sveltePreprocess()` transpiles `<script lang="ts">` blocks without performing TypeScript type-checking (that is exactly what `svelte-check` would add and what Decision 11 declines to add). So `npm run build` catches syntax errors and Svelte compiler errors, but not type errors inside components — e.g. a prop renamed in `groupTitle.ts`/`groupOrderUtils.ts` and not updated at a call site, or a callback signature drift between `BoardSettingsPopup.onSave` and `BoardHeader.saveSettings`, would not fail the build; Svelte silently ignores unknown/mistyped props at runtime. This isn't a defect in the spec — Decision 11 already names the gap and pins the burden on scenario coverage instead — but the coverage that actually catches it is narrower than 'build + tests' reads: Task 8 explicitly changes three call-signature links in the save chain and its own verify step is `npm run build && npm test` (unit only, no E2E), so a signature mismatch there would only surface in Wave 5/6 E2E, several tasks later.
findings.fix: No spec change required. Optional tightening: make Task 8's verify step also run the closest relevant E2E smoke (e.g. `core.spec.ts`) rather than deferring all save-chain verification to Wave 5/6, shortening the feedback loop for exactly the multi-signature change Decision 11 already flags as ungated by types.

summary: The major finding from round 1 is resolved correctly: Decision 3 now gives the popup row its own `data-settings-group` attribute, its rationale (popup and board coexist in the DOM — confirmed in App.svelte/BoardHeader.svelte, the overlay does not unmount BoardLayout) is accurate, and the wave split enforces the dependency structurally — Task 8 (Wave 4) introduces the attribute, Task 9 (Wave 5) migrates locators onto it, so the implicit same-wave contract from round 1 no longer exists. Tracing the wave graph confirms no unworkable intermediate state: `groupOrder` enters the data model in Wave 1 (Task 3) with a default equal to today's fixed order, so Wave 3 (Task 7, board reads `groupOrder`) renders identically to the pre-feature board even though the popup can't yet change it until Wave 4 — a safe, inert intermediate state, not a broken one. All three prior minor findings are now addressed as explicit, reasoned decisions (13: `groupTitles` vs. popup's local `title`; 14: accessibility/tab-order trade-off named as accepted; six-literal-block debt moved into the Risks table). Decision 4 (pure `groupTitle` helper over inline resolution) follows the codebase's existing precedent of `boardLayoutUtils.ts` and is the only way to unit-test the fallback rule given the Node-environment vitest config — a good fit, not a new pattern. Decision 11 (no `svelte-check`) is honestly reasoned and appropriately scoped out rather than smuggled in, though its practical gate is narrower than it reads (build catches syntax, not types) — flagged as a minor, non-blocking observation. No new critical or major issues found from the wave repartition; ready for task decomposition.
